timeline_reviews.summary: serial transport stream accounted for 4689 source events; no semantic ledger projection was used as task evidence.
Serial parent trajectory reviewed for local probing, local implementation, differential testing, and final delivery.

parallel.requirements: Port inflection-cpp tests/test15.cpp to Rust as a black-box equivalent, preserving stdout, stderr, exit behavior, byte handling, and deliverable layout.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent used workflow agents for black-box probing and later adversarial fuzzing, while retaining ownership of implementation, integration, rebuilds, and final delivery.
parallel.implementation: Parent created a Cargo project with inflection modules, raw argv handling, byte-wise pluralize/camelize/underscore/isPlural/demodulize behavior, and corrected isPlural after differential mismatch.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Parent wrote the source tree and binary entry point, rebuilt after edits, copied or produced the release executable, and left a coherent Rust artifact for evaluation.
parallel.verification: Parent ran local differential tests, observed an initial 14-mismatch isPlural gap, fixed it, reran pass=586 fail=0 checks, launched fuzzing, and confirmed a 25,255-case short full-diff had zero divergences.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No final task-relevant incorrect behavior is evidenced by the current official evaluation; background sweeps/workflows did not prevent a passing artifact.

serial.requirements: Port the same C++ driver and black-box inflection behavior to Rust, including raw-byte argv handling, naive rules, and abort-path parity.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Single parent performed all probing, implementation, verification, cleanup, and final response without delegation or subagent activity.
serial.implementation: Serial wrote Cargo.toml, test15.rs, and inflection modules with byte-vector APIs, exact word/suffix rule tables, and demodulize out-of-range behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Serial integrated all source under /output, built the release binary, cleaned temporary files, and reported the final layout.
serial.verification: Serial ran broad differential suites with 8,680 then 15,685 cases, explicit abort parity checks, Cargo binary spot checks, and a warning-free offline release build.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished or incorrect final behavior is evidenced; current official evaluation passed all 41 test cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Recognized the black-box C++ port requirement, byte-level behavior, Cargo deliverable, and official executable expectations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Recognized the same black-box port requirement and the need for raw-byte fidelity and C++ abort parity.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement gap; both reconstructed the inflection API behavior and delivered a Rust project that passed officially.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Delegated probing and fuzzing to workflows while the parent owned implementation, fixes, and final artifact assembly.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Kept probing, implementation, integration, testing, and closure in one serial parent trajectory without delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used child workflows to widen exploration; serial used a single-owner linear loop. Ownership of final implementation remained clear in both.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Workflow results supported behavior discovery, but the parent converted findings into one internally consistent Rust implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: All context remained local, with probes immediately informing the same actor that wrote and tested the code.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had handoff boundaries, but none produced lost, stale, conflicting, or unusably bulky information after parent synthesis.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parent wrote Cargo metadata, library modules, CLI handling, and test15 entry point, then fixed isPlural behavior after a diff mismatch.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote Cargo metadata and the inflection modules after local probing, including raw-byte rules and abort reproduction.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both converged on byte-level black-box parity; parallel needed a visible correction cycle while serial reached parity through local mapping.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent launched workflow children, observed results or progress, and did not depend on an unreturned child result for final delivery.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results; local command results were immediately consumed by the same actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had additional result lifecycle complexity, but no missing join, trapped verifier finding, or unused completed result changed the solution.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Final Rust files were written and reconciled by the parent in the output tree, with post-change rebuilds after rule edits.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Final Rust files were written by the serial parent in one workspace with no shared-agent write contention.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel child workflows did not create competing implementation files or overwrites; both final trees were coherent and buildable.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: After the initial mismatch, the parent rebuilt, reran differential checks, and launched adversarial/exhaustive verification before official pass.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran broad differential tests, abort parity checks, Cargo binary checks, and a warning-free release build before official pass.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had strong acceptance evidence. Parallel verification included workflow fuzzing plus parent local sweeps; serial verification was local but extensive.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran until agent timeout at process level, but already had a built passing artifact and local no-divergence evidence before evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed normally with remaining budget and final response after a clean build and verification summary.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent more budget on workflow fan-out and background sweeps, but this did not leave the deliverable incomplete or unverifiable.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcomes are not discordant: both current completed status evaluations passed 41 of 41 test cases. The concrete difference is that the parallel run used workflows for probe and fuzz breadth while the parent still owned implementation, repaired a discovered mismatch, and verified the final artifact; the serial run did the same task-solving loop locally without child-agent coordination.
parallel_contributors: Workflow probes and fuzzing broadened behavior discovery, but the parent remained the implementation and integration owner.
Parent local differential testing caught the isPlural mismatch and drove a corrective edit before final acceptance.
serial_contributors: Serial local probing kept context and implementation decisions in one actor.
Broad local differential and abort-path verification established byte-level parity before final response.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel initially had an ordinary isPlural rule defect that was detected and corrected before official evaluation.
Serial appears to have mapped the same rule family during local probing before its final broad verification pass.

candidates.reason: Rejected: background or timed-out child activity did not interrupt needed child work before a required result was finalized for the solution.
Rejected: no complete promotable candidate was left unplaced; the parent built and delivered the final Rust artifact.
Rejected: the material isPlural fix was followed by rebuilds and differential testing, not merged only after verification.
Rejected: no delegated implementation was completed and then left unjoined; implementation was parent-owned.
Rejected: no concrete verifier finding was trapped below the parent and needed for the final passing solution.
Rejected: when a mismatch appeared, the parent took over and corrected it before closure rather than leaving failed child scope unresolved.
Rejected: no available completed child result was ignored in a way that made the parent proceed inconsistently with it.
Rejected: the parent actively inspected progress and ran local verification; it did not simply wait until timeout while useful results sat available.
Rejected: there were no competing child-owned implementations across files that required adverse reconciliation.
Rejected: no two live agents edited the same source file with observed reconciliation or conflict.
Rejected: no source produced or actively owned by another agent was replaced as a harmful overwrite.
Rejected: the required entry point and executable were written by the parent, not overwritten from a competing live owner.
Rejected: no broad cleanup or promotion invalidated another agent final tree or provenance.
Rejected: multiple live agents did not write the shared implementation workspace in a way that caused unstable state or provenance loss.
Rejected: no generated child artifact, cache, fixture, or temporary path contaminated another actor as a false reference input.
